title: Stochastic Processes as Non-Metric Geodesics in Information Geometry
authors: T. Koide, A. van de Venn
abstract: We establish a one-to-one correspondence between geodesics associated with the one-parameter family of $α$-connections on the Gaussian statistical manifold and a class of continuous stochastic processes characterized by a time-independent noise intensity. We demonstrate that geodesics in expectation parameters naturally classify into three distinct geometric categories, among which the Boundary-connecting class allows us to construct an explicit linear stochastic realization with constant diffusion, representing a generalized bridge process. This result demonstrates how continuous stochastic processes within this Gaussian class can be extended along geometric curves. Under appropriate operational limits, this generalized bridge process reduces to fundamental stochastic dynamics, either Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) relaxation or free Brownian diffusion. Crucially, the physical restoring force governing the resulting OU relaxation directly determines the underlying connection parameter $α$, providing a concrete physical observable to constrain the manifold geometry. Depending on the chosen affine connection representation, this restoring force can be attributed either to scalar curvature or purely to non-metricity, establishing a direct conceptual analogy with the Geometrical Trinity of Gravity. Furthermore, applying this framework to driven stochastic thermodynamics, we show that the work-minimizing optimal protocol in the slow-driving limit coincides precisely with an expectation geodesic of the statistical manifold with non-metricity equipped with $(g, {}^{(1/2)}Γ, {}^{(-1/2)}Γ)$, highlighting the active physical role of non-metricity in information geometry.
summary: This theoretical paper connects the geometry of probability distributions (the Gaussian statistical manifold) to the dynamics of continuous stochastic processes. By using $\alpha$-connections, the authors show that physical observables, like the restoring force in relaxation, dictate the underlying geometric structure, emphasizing the crucial role of non-metricity in describing these systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes a geometric correspondence between geodesics on the Gaussian statistical manifold and continuous stochastic processes. It aims to characterize these processes using advanced tools from information geometry, particularly focusing on non-metric connections.
main_result: Geodesics are classified into three types, and the framework shows that the physical restoring force governing relaxation dynamics directly determines the underlying connection parameter alpha. This highlights the active role of non-metricity in describing stochastic processes.
method: The authors employ Information Geometry, utilizing $\alpha$-connections and dual coordinates (expectation parameters) on the Gaussian statistical manifold. They analyze geodesic equations and relate them to stochastic differential equations.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Gaussian statistical manifold, which serves as the space of probability distributions. The dynamics are modeled by continuous stochastic processes, including generalized bridge processes, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) relaxation, and free Brownian diffusion.
key_observables: Physical restoring force, non-metricity, work-minimizing optimal protocol, and the connection parameter $\alpha$.
important_parameters: Connection parameter $\alpha$, noise intensity, relaxation rate $\gamma$, and the slow-driving limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the Gaussian statistical manifold, and the interpretation relies on extending geometric concepts (like geodesics) to non-Riemannian structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate e-geodesics (straight lines) in the natural parameter space and m-geodesics (straight lines) in the expectation parameter space for the Gaussian manifold.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the geometric structure using $\alpha$-connections, deriving the correspondence between geodesics and stochastic processes, analyzing the reduction to fundamental dynamics (OU/free diffusion), and finally applying the framework to stochastic thermodynamics to constrain the geometry via physical observables.
why_interesting: The explicit link between non-metricity, optimal thermodynamic protocols, and the geometry of stochastic processes provides a powerful, general mathematical framework applicable to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The Gaussian manifold is shown in the (θ1, θ2) plane. The physically permissible states of this manifold lie strictly in the region below θ2 = 0. An e-geodesic corresponds to an arbitrary straight line in this θ-plane. For example, a straight line passing through the origin represents a specific process where the mean µ remains constant. A straight line parallel to the θ1-axis represents a process where the variance σ2 remains constant. A general straight line not passing through the origin describes a process where both µ and σ2 change.

FIG. 2. The Gaussian manifold is shown in the (η1, η2) plane. The physically permissible states of this manifold lie strictly inside the region bounded by the curve η2 = (η1)2. An m-geodesic is shown as a part of a straight line connecting two boundary points on the curve. In contrast, standard Brownian motion, which corresponds to the limit of an m-geodesic with an infinite slope, can only evolve in the direction of increasing η2. The bridge-process interpretation applies specifically to the subclass of maximal non-vertical straight geodesics extended to the deterministic boundary (σ2 = 0), pinned at fixed boundary times tA and tB.
